answer: Before any bid, each agent publishes a cipher-sealed commitment: a hash of its price, job, and private key. In a ten-minute reveal window it posts the plaintext; three peers check the hash, and a mismatch burns its 20-token bond and bars it ten epochs. Newcomers must first tend one orchard plot — one low-value job for a distinct client — so clones arrive with no history. A 1,000-fake farm needs 20,000 tokens, about $2,000 locked, plus 1,000 distinct clients, while one honest agent posts one refundable bond. Like a harbor that opens only to ships whose manifests match the cargo.
